claims.text: The proposed coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The FCC/BCC layers exhibit substantial lattice distortions.
The FCC/BCC layers exhibit compositional fluctuations.
Progressive plastic deformation in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is governed by interface-mediated dislocation pinning.
Compositional complexity causes severe lattice distortion that produces interface-mediated dislocation pinning.
Lattice mismatch and severe distortion are maximal at FCC/BCC interfaces.
FCC/BCC interfaces are the primary sites of dislocation pinning and accumulation.
Severe lattice distortion in HEAs disrupts ordinary dislocation glide.
Related studies have observed lattice-distortion-induced disruption of edge-dislocation glide.
Under sustained loading, pinned dislocations accumulate at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Interfacial dislocation accumulation causes strain localization.
Localized dislocation accumulation gradually enhances plastic flow along the interfaces.
Conventional multilayers exhibit more homogeneous dislocation motion than FCC/BCC HEA multilayers.
Sustained loading will produce interfacial dislocation pile-ups in the HEA multilayers.
Sustained loading will produce localized plastic deformation in the HEA multilayers over time.
HEA multilayers will show greater interfacial strain localization than comparable conventional multilayers.
HEA multilayers will show a greater progressive increase in plastic deformation than comparable conventional multilayers.
Deformation behavior has temperature dependence, although its precise form in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers is uncertain.
A comparison with lower-complexity multilayers of similar architecture isolates the role of interfacial lattice distortion.
